To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

15% of patients reported a delayed first consultation after HIV infection diagnosis, with a higher proportion of women living in a couple, patients diagnosed during voluntary screening campaigns, patients with a negative perception of antiviral treatment toxicity, and patients consulting HIV care centers located in small or middle-size hospitals and created before the decentralization of HIV diagnosis.

the full implementation of decentralization of care in Cameroon was associated with a significant reduction in the proportion of individuals reporting a delay in first consultation after HIV testing, but that a significant proportion of patients (15%) reported a delay of more than 6 months.

1) the national antiretoviral treatment (ART) scale-up program in Cameroon has reduced the delay before first consultation after HIV infection diagnosis; 2) the characteristics of the health care center providing HIV care and the circumstances of diagnosis are associated with delayed first consultation; and 3) counseling on the balance between the effectiveness and side effects of antiretrovirals is a key factor for reducing the delay before first HIV consultation in Cameroon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of decentralization of HIV/AIDS care in the context of antiretrovirals scale-up program on the time between HIV diagnosis and first consultation in HIV care centers in Cameroon.

the study of the impact of the decentralisation of care on the delay before the first consultation after the diagnosis of HIV infection, in the context in the national antiretoviral treatment scale-up programme in Cameroon.
understanding the impact of decentralization of care on the time to first consultation after HIV infection diagnosis in Cameroon.

the results from this study are useful to understand and to improve the care of patients living with HIV/AIDS in Cameroon.
the national antiretovirals treatment scale-up program has reduced the delays before the first consultation for HIV-infected patients in Cameroon.

the study results underline the importance of coordination between diagnosis and treatment activities and the importance of developing counselling actions, focusing on both the balance between antiviral effectiveness and its potential toxicity and the importance of counselling as an integral part of the patients follow-up after diagnosis, during voluntary screening campaigns, in Cameroon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is still a delay of 6 months before the first consultation of HIV patients in Cameroon.
the decentralization of HIV services has reduced delays before first consultation, but that the quality of care and patient's perceptions of antiretrovirals need improvement.

in Cameroon, the national scale-up of antiretrovirals treatment (ART) has led to a reduction of delays before first consultation for care, but that some patients still report a long period between HIV diagnosis and their first visit to a HIV center.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important to provide HIV testing and counseling services at the same location and at the same time, so that patients can get the results of their HIV test immediately and be referred to HIV care services if needed.
we have shown that the decentralization strategy in Cameroon has reduced delays before first consultation.
we should continue to decentralize HIV care to reduce delays in first consultation.
